description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, crispy on the outside and tender inside, packed with a delightful medley of fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of savory flavors and satisfying textures, making it an irresistible appetizer or a light meal. Served with a tangy soy-based dipping sauce, it’s a culinary experience that captures the essence of Korean comfort food.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Clean and prepare all seafood. Chop shrimp and squid into bite-sized pieces. Thinly slice the onion and red chili. Trim green onions and cut them into approximately 3-4 inch lengths. Keep a small portion of green onions aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Mix the Pancake Batter
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, and black pepper. Gradually add the cold water or anchovy broth, whisking continuously until the batter is smooth and lump-free. Stir in the large egg until it is well combined. Avoid overmixing the batter.

instructions.title: Combine Ingredients for Pancake
instructions.text: Gently fold the prepared seafood, sliced onion, and about two-thirds of the cut green onion pieces into the pancake batter. Mix just enough to evenly distribute the ingredients without crushing them, ensuring everything is coated.

instructions.title: Heat the Frying Pan
instructions.text: Place a large non-stick skillet or a cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of cooking oil to the pan, ensuring it coats the entire bottom surface. Heat until the oil is shimmering and just starting to smoke, indicating it is hot enough.

instructions.title: Cook the First Side of Pancake
instructions.text: Pour about 1.5 to 2 cups of the batter mixture into the hot pan, spreading it out evenly with a spatula to form a round pancake. Immediately arrange the remaining green onion pieces decoratively on top of the batter. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the bottom is beautifully golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Flip and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Drizzle a little more oil around the edges of the pancake. Carefully use a large spatula to flip the pancake over. Press down gently with the spatula to ensure even contact with the pan. Continue to cook for another 5-7 minutes until the other side is golden brown and crispy, and the seafood is thoroughly cooked through.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: While the pancake is cooking, prepare the dipping sauce. In a small bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, minced garlic, and a pinch of red pepper flakes (gochugaru) until well combined.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the freshly cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Slice it into wedges or squares. Serve the hot and crispy pancake immediately with the prepared tangy dipping sauce on the side. Enjoy this delightful Korean treat!

tips: For an extra crispy pancake, use very cold water or even ice water when making the batter. This helps to inhibit gluten development.
Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook one pancake at a time to ensure even cooking and a perfectly crispy texture.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking to enjoy its optimal crispiness and warmth. It is best fresh.
For a deeper umami flavor, consider using anchovy broth (dashima-gukmul) instead of plain water in your pancake batter.
article:
Haemul Pajeon: The Ultimate Guide to Making Korean Seafood Pancake

Imagine a rainy day, the gentle patter of raindrops outside, and the comforting aroma of sizzling savory delights filling your kitchen. For many Koreans, this scene is perfectly complemented by a plate of Haemul Pajeon, the quintessential Korean Seafood Pancake. More than just a dish, it's a culinary experience – a crispy-edged, chewy-centered, umami-rich pancake packed with fresh seafood and vibrant green onions. Beloved as a snack, an appetizer, or a hearty accompaniment to a glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine), Haemul Pajeon offers a delightful journey into the heart of Korean comfort food. If you've ever savored its unique texture and flavor at a Korean restaurant, you'll be thrilled to discover how simple it is to recreate this authentic taste at home.

## What is Haemul Pajeon (Korean Seafood Pancake)?

Haemul Pajeon literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake," and that name perfectly encapsulates its essence. It's a type of "jeon," a broad category of Korean pan-fried dishes made from various ingredients coated in a flour and egg batter. What sets Haemul Pajeon apart is its generous use of fresh seafood and long strands of green onions, which are often laid out dramatically before being enveloped in a light, savory batter.

The magic of this dish lies in its contrasts. The exterior boasts a golden, crispy crunch, often achieved through generous oil and high heat, while the interior remains wonderfully soft and tender. Each bite delivers a burst of briny seafood flavor, complemented by the slightly pungent sweetness of the green onions and the savory depth of the batter. It's a dish that embodies both simplicity and sophistication, making it a perennial favorite in Korean households and restaurants worldwide. Traditionally enjoyed on rainy days because the sizzling sound of the pancake on the griddle is said to mimic the sound of rain, it’s also a popular choice for celebrations and casual gatherings.

## Ingredients for Korean Seafood Pancake

Creating an authentic Korean Seafood Pancake starts with selecting the right ingredients. Freshness is key, especially when it comes to the seafood, which forms the heart of this dish.

For the Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour
*   2 tablespoons cornstarch (for extra crispiness)
*   1 large egg
*   1 ½ cups ice water or cold broth (vegetable or anchovy broth adds depth)
*   ½ teaspoon salt
*   Pinch of black pepper

For the Fillings:
*   1 ½ cups mixed seafood, chopped into bite-sized pieces (shrimp, squid rings, mussels, bay scallops are excellent choices)
*   1 bunch green onions (about 8-10 stalks), cut into 2-3 inch lengths
*   Optional: ¼ cup thinly sliced onion, ¼ cup shredded carrot, a few sliced shiitake mushrooms for added flavor and texture.

For Frying:
*   ¼ cup vegetable oil or any neutral oil (you might need more)

For the Dipping Sauce (essential!):
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon rice vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   ½ teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional)
*   1 clove garlic, minced
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   A few thin slices of green onion (from the white part)

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Haemul Pajeon

Making a delicious Korean Seafood Pancake is surprisingly straightforward. Follow these steps for a perfect result every time:

1.  **Prepare the Dipping Sauce:** In a small bowl, combine all dipping sauce ingredients. Stir well and set aside to allow the flavors to meld.
2.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:** If using frozen seafood, thaw it completely and pat it very dry with paper towels to prevent a watery pancake. Cut larger pieces into bite-sized portions. Wash and trim the green onions, then cut them into 2-3 inch segments. Prepare any optional vegetables.
3.  **Make the Batter:** In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, salt, and pepper. In a separate bowl, lightly beat the egg, then add the ice water or broth. Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are fine; do not overmix, as this can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should be slightly thicker than crepe batter, able to coat the back of a spoon. Using ice water helps create a crispier pancake.
4.  **Heat the Pan:** Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of oil, ensuring it coats the bottom of the pan evenly. The oil should be shimmering but not smoking.
5.  **Assemble and Cook the Pancake:**
    *   Pour about ½ cup of batter into the hot pan, spreading it thinly to form a round pancake (about 6-8 inches in diameter).
    *   Quickly arrange a generous layer of green onion pieces over the batter.
    *   Distribute a portion of the mixed seafood evenly over the green onions. If using, add other vegetables.
    *   Spoon a little more batter (about 1-2 tablespoons) over the seafood and green onions, just enough to bind them.
    *   Reduce the heat to medium. Cook for 3-5 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges begin to set.
    *   Carefully flip the pancake. You might need to add a little more oil around the edges to help it crisp up. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until the second side is golden brown and the seafood is cooked through.
6.  **Serve Immediately:** Transfer the Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and slice it into wedges or squares. Serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat the process for the remaining batter and ingredients.

## Pro Tips for the Best Korean Seafood Pancake

Achieving that perfect balance of crispy exterior and tender interior in your Korean Seafood Pancake takes a little finesse. Here are some pro tips to elevate your homemade version:

*   **Don't Skimp on Oil:** A common mistake is using too little oil. For truly crispy edges, you need a generous amount of oil, especially when you flip the pancake. The oil helps to fry the batter rather than just cook it.
*   **Ice Water is Your Friend:** Using very cold water, or even ice water, for your batter helps inhibit gluten development, resulting in a lighter, crisper pancake.
*   **Batter Consistency:** The batter should be pourable but not watery. If it's too thick, your pancake will be gummy. If it's too thin, it won't hold together. Adjust with a tablespoon of flour or water if needed.
*   **Plenty of Green Onions:** The "pa" in Pajeon is crucial! Don't be shy with the green onions. They provide a fresh, slightly pungent flavor and a delightful texture.
*   **High Heat Start:** Begin with medium-high heat to get that initial sizzle and crispiness, then reduce it slightly to medium to ensure the inside cooks through without burning the outside.
*   **Even Distribution:** Spread your seafood and green onions evenly across the pancake for balanced flavor and texture in every bite.
*   **Serve Hot:** Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed immediately off the pan when it's piping hot and at its crispiest.

## Serving Suggestions for Haemul Pajeon

Haemul Pajeon is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in various ways:

*   **As an Appetizer:** It makes a fantastic starter for any Korean meal, whetting the appetite with its savory goodness.
*   **Light Meal or Snack:** Paired with a simple side salad or some kimchi, it can be a satisfying light lunch or an afternoon snack.
*   **With Makgeolli or Soju:** This is perhaps the most classic pairing. The slightly sweet, effervescent makgeolli (Korean rice wine) cuts through the richness of the Korean Seafood Pancake beautifully, especially on a rainy day. Soju also makes an excellent companion.
*   **Part of a Feast:** Serve it alongside other Korean staples like bulgogi, bibimbap, or various banchan (side dishes) for a complete and delicious Korean feast.
*   **The Dipping Sauce:** Never forget the dipping sauce! Its tangy, savory, and slightly spicy notes perfectly complement the rich pancake.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Haemul Pajeon is a culinary delight, there are many ways to customize this dish to suit your preferences or what you have on hand:

*   **Vegetarian Pajeon:** Omit the seafood entirely and load up on vegetables like mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, enoki), zucchini, bell peppers, carrots, and onions. You can also add crumbled tofu for protein.
*   **Kimchi Pajeon (Kimchijeon):** A very popular variation! Simply chop up some ripe kimchi and add it to the batter. The fermented tang of kimchi adds incredible depth and a spicy kick.
*   **Meat Pajeon:** For meat lovers, finely sliced beef (bulgogi-style), pork, or chicken can be used instead of or in addition to seafood.
*   **Different Flours:** While all-purpose flour is standard, you can experiment with a blend of rice flour and wheat flour for a chewier texture, or even a small amount of buckwheat flour for an earthy note.
*   **Spicy Kick:** If you love heat, add a teaspoon of gochujang (Korean chili paste) or extra gochugaru to the batter. You can also add sliced fresh chilies (like serrano or jalapeño) to the pancake for a vibrant heat.
*   **Other Seafood:** Feel free to use any combination of your favorite seafood: clams, scallops, oysters, crab meat (real or imitation), or even tuna from a can (drained well).

Haemul Pajeon is more than just a pancake; it's a celebration of fresh ingredients and simple cooking techniques that yield incredibly satisfying results. Whether you're a seasoned Korean food enthusiast or a curious newcomer, making your own Korean Seafood Pancake at home is a rewarding experience. It's a dish that brings warmth, comfort, and a burst of authentic Korean flavor to any table. So, next time the craving strikes, or the rain starts to fall, gather your ingredients and get ready to sizzle up a batch of this irresistible Korean classic.
